summary: Tested Multiplier free-input + warning/error/disable, Payments summary drill-down, Team KPI drill-down, and regressions. Critical blocker found: /payments page crashes with a runtime ReferenceError (`breakdown is not defined`) caused by a missing `useState` declaration in /app/frontend/src/pages/Payments.js. Because the Payments page does not mount, four of the five requested test areas could NOT be exercised on that page (multiplier modal from Payments, payments summary drill-down, payment-detail modal regression, generate-link regression). The same multiplier logic, however, is shared with LeadDetail's PaymentModal and was fully verified there. Team KPI drill-down (admin) works for all 4 KPIs.

ui_bugs.issue: Runtime crash: `ReferenceError: breakdown is not defined`. setBreakdown(...) is called inside openBreakdown() and `breakdown?.title / breakdown?.list / !!breakdown` are read in JSX, but the corresponding `const [breakdown, setBreakdown] = useState(null);` declaration is missing from the component (all other useState lines exist around lines 85-98). The page renders the red runtime overlay instead of the UI on every load. Confirmed via grep: setBreakdown referenced 3x (lines 216, 218, 220) and a setBreakdown(null) onClose (line 257), but no `const [breakdown, ...]` declaration anywhere.

action_items: FIX CRITICAL (one-liner): in /app/frontend/src/pages/Payments.js, add `const [breakdown, setBreakdown] = useState(null);` alongside the other useState hooks (around line 97). This single missing declaration crashes the entire Payments route and blocks 4 of the 5 features in this iteration.

After the fix, re-test on /payments: (a) New Payment Link → pay-multiplier number input behaviour at 7.5/9/16/10 and generate-payment-btn disabled state at >15, (b) pay-summary-collected/pending/links open payments-breakdown-modal with payments-breakdown-table + breakdown-row-{id}, (c) clicking a pay-row-{id} still opens payment-detail-modal, (d) generating a valid Razorpay link at multiplier 7.5 fires the success toast and clipboard copy.

Minor UX (non-blocking): TeamStatModal in /app/frontend/src/pages/Team.js does NOT close on Escape key (it's a custom div-overlay, not the shared Modal). Backdrop click + ✕ button both work. Consider adding an Escape keydown handler for parity with the other modals.
critical_code_review_comments: Payments.js — missing useState declaration for `breakdown` while setBreakdown/breakdown are referenced. This is a clear oversight that would have been caught by `react/no-undef` / `no-undef` ESLint rule had it been enforced; recommend adding a pre-commit lint step.

TeamStatModal is a hand-rolled overlay instead of using the shared Modal primitive used elsewhere (PaymentModal, PaymentsBreakdownModal). This causes inconsistent behaviour (no Escape-to-close, no focus trap). Refactor to use the shared Modal for consistency.

rca of the issue: RCA: /app/frontend/src/pages/Payments.js declares state for q, results, loading, payments, fxRate, rateInput, savingRate, meta, packages, pickerOpen, payOpen, linkLead, linkTarget, detail, payForm — but the new `breakdown` state introduced for the drill-down feature was never declared. The handler `openBreakdown(kind)` (line 214) calls `setBreakdown(...)`, and the JSX (line 257) reads `!!breakdown`, `breakdown?.title`, `breakdown?.list`, `setBreakdown(null)`. At module-evaluation/render time React throws `ReferenceError: breakdown is not defined`, which bubbles up and renders the Uncaught runtime errors overlay. Reproduction: log in via Demo View → click Payments in the sidebar (or visit /payments). Mitigation: add `const [breakdown, setBreakdown] = useState(null);` near the other useState lines (~line 97/98) in Payments.js. Service restart not needed (hot reload).
